# ConnectBot Termlib 0.3.15 source overlay

This module builds the source/resources from [ConnectBot Termlib 0.3.15](https://github.com/connectbot/termlib/tree/7a50d641ec92ef164645af1f4e39d0bf1a86b480), commit `7a50d641ec92ef164645af1f4e39d0bf1a86b480`. `ImeInputView.kt` supplies the normal terminal keyboard profile. The local rendered-link hit-test is in `RenderedTerminalLink.kt` and `StrictTerminalLink.kt`, wired through `Terminal.kt`, `TerminalLine.kt` and `PackedCells.kt`. The one-shot keyboard bridge adds the narrow `TerminalKeySink` and `TransactionalModifierManager` APIs, uses ordered encoded input in `TerminalEmulator.kt`, and consumes held bits only after Pocket acknowledges exact-PTY enqueue. The upstream `consumer-rules.pro`, JVM sources and Android resources were imported directly from `lib`.

The Gradle script uses the regular Android library plug-in to compile these sources. Its separate non-transitive Maven configuration fetches the official `org.connectbot:termlib:0.3.15@aar`; the checked SHA-256 is `85276764f139bc8457918dbfff8a4e3fd22da9b500e4569d2d882f37d67f8e57`. Only the original arm64 `jni/arm64-v8a/libjni_cb_term.so` is extracted into a generated source directory. No compiled implementation classes are taken from that AAR, overwritten, or shipped alongside the source module. No native toolchain, runtime patching, or runtime download is needed.

The terminal-only editor declares the normal Android text layout with no predictive suggestions and requests no personalized learning. It still uses raw PTY dispatch, not Termlib's composer mode. Android's BaseInputConnection fallback key synthesis is disabled independently of Termlib's composer flag: framework editing operates only on the temporary IME span. It never supplies already-sent PTY text as Android editor history. Provisional IME text is not sent merely because the editor is dismissed or finished, and edits to that provisional text do not generate remote backspaces. Explicit IME commits and ordinary editing keys keep the existing terminal decoder/renderer owner checks. Android IMEs can still provide their own layouts and may not honor optional hints.

On update, import the upstream JVM/resource directories and consumer rules again, rebase the marked IME/viewport patches, update the Maven pin and checksum together, and rerun app build/tests/lint, JNI linkage/payload checks and a handset keyboard smoke test. Upstream Apache-2.0 and bundled libvterm MIT licenses are preserved in the app's `src/main/assets/{TERMLIB,LIBVTERM}-LICENSE.txt` and packaged into the APK.
